issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a function named simulate_msd_one_round(n_shots: int, p: float) but the template defines simulate_one_round(...) (different name). This name/signature mismatch is structural: students following the template will not find the expected simulate_msd_one_round symbol to implement or tests expecting that name will fail to import it. The template also contains a NotImplementedError message referencing simulate_msd_one_round while the actual function is named simulate_one_round, which is internally inconsistent and confusing.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function simulate_one_round to simulate_msd_one_round with the same parameter order (n_shots: int, p: float). Also update the NotImplementedError message to match the actual function name, or alternatively add a wrapper function simulate_msd_one_round that calls simulate_one_round to preserve backward compatibility. Ensure tests and plot helpers call the same name consistently.

issues.description: The template implementation declares a function named simulate_one_round but the problem statement and the solution implementation refer to simulate_msd_one_round. Additionally, the template's plot_msd calls simulate_msd_one_round while the declared name is simulate_one_round. This mismatched identifier will confuse students and causes runtime/name errors when following the problem text or running provided plotting/test code.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function simulate_one_round to simulate_msd_one_round (or add a small wrapper alias simulate_msd_one_round = simulate_one_round) and ensure all internal calls (e.g., plot_msd) use the same identifier so the problem statement, template, and solution consistently reference simulate_msd_one_round.
